problem: Hierarchical open-vocabulary object navigation (scene/room/region/instance-level goals) needs persistent room-level spatial evidence and clear candidate views, but prior methods either need complete 3D scans or passively accumulate incidental, viewpoint-biased observations, and verify candidates from possibly distant, occluded or uninformative views.
motivation: Real users give goals like 'the red bottle in my bedroom', mixing category, room context and attributes. Room semantics is a holistic property that needs wide views, and instance attributes need discriminative close views, neither of which passive exploration guarantees. So the agent should actively acquire observations for both grounding and verification.
key_idea: Apply active perception at two stages in a zero-shot online navigator: build a queryable room-semantic BEV representation from actively captured holistic room snapshots (QSSR), and reposition to informative viewpoints before verifying candidates (AVV).
insight: Room semantics from actively captured holistic snapshots is more reliable than from passive single views: the ablation with only the sub-room field S3 gives Room SR 39.4 versus 45.8 for S1+S2 and 47.7 for the full model. For AVV, target verification gives the largest gain and viewpoint selection improves SR further but lowers SPL (VS+TV 39.2/17.6 vs TV 36.0/19.2 on single-goal). The sufficiency evaluation triggers repositioning only when needed, which recovers efficiency (full model 39.6/19.9).
method: Online Room Segmentation (S1): partitions explored free space on the online obstacle map into room instances using door boundaries, accumulating door projections over a window of m frames; doors also give the inward direction for snapshots.

Active Room Perception (S2): captures stitched room snapshots (N_v frames rotating in place) at initialization, first entry to a room, and on substantial room-area expansion; a VLM classifies each snapshot into room types C_k, and the snapshots V_k are kept as visual evidence.

Sub-Room Semantic Refinement (S3): a Places scene encoder gives patch-level room-type logits restricted to an indoor vocabulary, back-projected and summed over time into a BEV probability field Phi to separate functional areas in open or under-segmented rooms.

Spatial Semantic Query: for a detected candidate, uses its BEV footprint to take the room type (argmax of mean Phi over C_k if there are multiple types), and uses VQA over V_k to check region descriptions, filtering spatially inconsistent candidates.
AVV Sufficiency Evaluation: a VLM scores visibility and perspective (1-5 each) from the candidate crop plus the full image; if the sum s < tau the agent repositions.

AVV Viewpoint Selection: samples 24 angles on rings of radius 0.8-2.4 m around the footprint median, filters by navigability and an adaptive minimum distance from the vertical FoV, and picks the viewpoint with max ray-cast visibility on a 2.5D height map; at most 3 attempts, then uses the best-scoring view.

Target Verification: the VLM checks category on the highlighted candidate in context, and an LLM-parsed attribute list is checked for instance-level goals; rejected candidates are blacklisted and VLFM-style frontier exploration resumes.

setting.backbone: Qwen2.5-VL-7B, Qwen3.5-9B (thinking), Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-thinking, GPT-4o (all frozen VLMs); GroundingDINO + SAM; Places scene encoder; VLFM frontier exploration
setting.observation: egocentric RGB-D + odometry (initial panorama and in-place rotation snapshots)

results: With Qwen3-VL-235B-A22B-thinking, SAP-Nav reaches 39.6 SR / 19.9 SPL on LangMap single-goal, above the best training-based PlaNaVid (31.4/15.2) and training-free 3D-Mem (21.2/8.7), and is best at every granularity. On HM3D-OVON val unseen it attains the top SR of 49.7 (vs MetaNav 46.1 and NavFoM 45.2), but its SPL of 23.1 is below NavFoM (31.9) and MetaNav (29.8).
limitations: AVV picks viewpoints by geometric visibility only, ignoring semantic utility and motion cost, which lowers SPL.
QSSR is not kept across tasks, so there is no lifelong memory reuse.
Instance-level performance stays low (about 26.8 SR), and results depend heavily on VLM scale (Qwen2.5-VL-7B is much weaker).
